subject: Weekly leadership heatcheck: OKR signal lights + QBR ready list
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly leadership heatcheck: OKR signal lights + QBR ready list

Team —
Quick weekly check-in ahead of QBR planning next week. Short bullets (intent: highlight where we need decisions or help).

Wins
- Hosted API latency P50 improved 12% week-over-week after kernel tuning; customer A/B tests show 8% drop in tail-latency complaints. (slide 2 in attached PDF)
- Two proof-of-concepts converted to committed pilots: Ava Analytics signed MOU for Dedicated pool (deal in Hub: AVA-4897).

Risks
- Dedicated capacity availability: expected ramp for committed pilots (Ava, one other) strains our 8xGPU pool in us-west. If we don't increase burst capacity or shift some workloads to quantized variants, we will miss the SLA target for peak windows.
- QBR metric gap: embedding unit cost normalization is still not applied across models; finance will flag this in the pack unless we reconcile by Wednesday.

Asks / Actions
1) Markus: can you approve a one-week burst add (2x A100 equivalent) for us-west? This is temporary and budgeted from the sales acceleration kitty — response needed by Tue EOD.
2) Maya: prioritize the embedding reconciliation task and confirm it's done by Tue noon so I can fold numbers into QBR deck.
3) Laura: do we want to escalate an interim SLA note to the customer list (Ava)? If so, I can draft a short proactive message.

Attachments: QBR_Prep_Slate_v2.pdf (deck), OKR-dashboard-2027Q3.csv (raw numbers)

Thanks — short and actionable please.

Jonas Weber
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership heatcheck: OKR signal lights + QBR ready list

Jonas —
Thanks for the concise rundown. A couple quick responses:
- I support a one-week burst to avoid customer impact. Markus, please advise on cost/approval cadence.
- On the embedding normalization: Maya, if you can confirm the adjusted numbers by Tue noon I will slot them into the executive summary. If there's any material change to forecasted SOPC, flag it and we'll rebase.

Also recommend we do not proactively message customers until we have the patch plan for latency — proactively notifying without a mitigation can cause more churn. If we must notify, keep language high-level and include a target remediation window.

Laura Bennett
COO, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 12:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership heatcheck: OKR signal lights + QBR ready list

Quick note on Dedicated capacity — flagging a specific operational constraint: the current autoscaler requires a 48-hour lead to spin a second static pod pool with the compliance wrap for Dedicated. That means an approval today/tomorrow is insufficient to cover a customer spike expected this Thursday. Two mitigation options:
- Short-term: move Ava's non-latency-critical batch jobs to a quantized variant in the regional shared pool (fast to implement, small accuracy delta).
- Medium-term: approve and provision the burst now (we can expedite but we still need an ops window for compliance checks).

If we go with short-term shift, engineering can deploy a rollout by Wednesday EOD. If we need the full Dedicated SLA for the pilot, we must expedite approval by EOD Monday and accept a limited implementation risk.

Action asked: leadership to confirm mitigation preference (short-term shim vs. expedite burst). If no decision by Mon 9am, ops will proceed with the safer short-term shift.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Thanks all — quick status and next steps:
- Markus: signage to approve a short burst. Markus, can you confirm approval by Mon 09:00PT? If approved, ops will fire provisioning flows immediately; Vivek, please instrument a reduced risk checklist. Attach: capacity-deck-slide6.png
- Maya: I have a placeholder in the deck for the embedding normalization; please push numbers to the shared Drive link and ping Laura when done.
- Customer comms: per Laura, we will not proactively message Ava until we have a patch plan. However, I'm copying their engineering contact so they're aware we're monitoring and prioritizing (no SLA language or changes in this thread).

I'll update the QBR slate with any figures we get tomorrow AM. If anyone needs me to present the operational slides for QBR, say so — I can prepare a 5-min talk track.

Jonas Weber
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
